items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening prepositional phrase
items.stem: The leaves of the desert plant ___ during the dry season.
items.answer_explanation: The past-tense verb agrees with the plural subject leaves and the completed-time context.

distractor_rationales.A: The present form does not match the completed-time context.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: wilted agrees with leaves in the past-tense clause.
distractor_rationales.C: The singular present form does not agree with leaves.
distractor_rationales.D: The participle cannot serve as the finite verb here.

items.subtype: embedded question with statement word order
items.stem: Researchers have not determined ___ the ancient temple was built.
items.answer_explanation: An embedded question uses statement order: when the temple was built.

distractor_rationales.A: Inversion is not used in an embedded question.
distractor_rationales.B: Do-inversion is not used after determined.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: when introduces the embedded clause with statement order.
distractor_rationales.D: That cannot introduce this embedded question meaningfully.

items.subtype: restrictive relative clause with object relative marker
items.stem: The wetlands ___ the university restored now attract many birds.
items.answer_explanation: That is the object relative marker in the restrictive clause.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: that replaces the object of restored.
distractor_rationales.B: The extra subject creates a double-object structure.
distractor_rationales.C: The extra they makes the relative clause ungrammatical.
distractor_rationales.D: The participle does not form the intended finite relative clause.

items.subtype: conditional clause with a finite subordinate clause
items.stem: ___ the storm weakens, coastal residents will remain indoors.
items.answer_explanation: If introduces the condition for the result clause.

distractor_rationales.A: Because expresses cause, not the stated condition.
distractor_rationales.B: Although expresses contrast rather than a condition.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: if introduces the conditional subordinate clause.

items.subtype: contrast connector followed by a finite clause
items.stem: The proposal was expensive, ___ the council approved it.
items.answer_explanation: But correctly coordinates two contrasting independent clauses.

distractor_rationales.B: Because gives a cause and cannot coordinate these ideas as intended.
distractor_rationales.D: So that introduces purpose or result.

items.subtype: passive voice in a completed research process
items.stem: Before publication, the alloy samples ___ by three independent laboratories.
items.answer_explanation: Had been tested expresses a completed passive process before publication.

distractor_rationales.A: The simple past omits the earlier-completion relationship.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: had been tested is past perfect passive.
distractor_rationales.C: The active present perfect has the wrong voice and time.
distractor_rationales.D: The progressive active form has the wrong voice.

items.subtype: causative verb followed by object and predicate adjective
items.stem: The new trees will make the avenue ___.
items.answer_explanation: Make takes an object followed by a predicate adjective describing it.

distractor_rationales.A: The bare noun/verb form is not the required predicate adjective.
distractor_rationales.B: The participle does not fit the selected complement frame.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: shady is the predicate adjective after make the avenue.
distractor_rationales.D: This adverb cannot function as the predicate complement.

items.subtype: reduced passive relative clause with a past participle
items.stem: The fragments ___ in the crater were preserved for analysis.
items.answer_explanation: To discover is the infinitive form required by the intended reduced construction.

distractor_rationales.A: The active participle gives the fragments an implausible agent role.
distractor_rationales.B: The past participle creates a different reduced passive reading.
distractor_rationales.C: A finite clause cannot fill this reduced phrase position.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct for the planned infinitive construction.

items.subtype: so plus adjective licensing a result that-clause
items.stem: The chamber was ___ that even a whisper could be recorded clearly.
items.answer_explanation: Such quiet is the planned degree expression licensing the following that result clause.

distractor_rationales.A: So normally requires an adjective phrase, not the planned noun phrase construction.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct for the selected such-plus-noun result construction.
distractor_rationales.C: An adverb cannot serve as the complement of was here.
distractor_rationales.D: As quiet requires a comparison complement.

items.subtype: not only plus coordinated parallel verb phrases
items.stem: The exhibit not only informs visitors but also ___.
items.answer_explanation: The two coordinated complements are parallel finite verb phrases.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: entertains them parallels informs visitors.
distractor_rationales.B: The participle is not parallel to the finite verb.
distractor_rationales.C: A noun is not parallel to the verb phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: The infinitive is not parallel to the finite verb.

items.subtype: appositive noun phrase after a proper noun
items.stem: Maya Chen, ___, presented the findings at the conference.
items.answer_explanation: The appositive noun phrase follows the proper name and identifies Maya Chen.

distractor_rationales.A: The adjective is misplaced after the noun in this phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: The word order does not form an appositive noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: a respected sociolinguist is a well-formed appositive.
distractor_rationales.D: The determiner and noun order is incorrect.

items.subtype: subject-auxiliary inversion after a fronted negative adverbial
items.stem: Never before ___ such a significant amendment been proposed.
items.answer_explanation: The fronted negative adverbial requires inversion of the auxiliary and subject.

distractor_rationales.B: The inserted phrase disrupts the required inversion.
distractor_rationales.C: It adds a subject that is not part of the intended clause.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: it has follows the fronted negative adverbial in the planned order.

items.subtype: there plus be with a postposed plural noun phrase
items.stem: There ___ several underground streams beneath the valley.
items.answer_explanation: The plural postposed noun phrase streams requires are.

distractor_rationales.A: Is does not agree with the plural noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: are agrees with several streams.
distractor_rationales.C: The bare form cannot be the finite verb here.
distractor_rationales.D: The participle cannot serve as the finite verb.

items.subtype: quantifier selected for an uncountable academic noun
items.stem: The report provides ___ information about regional employment trends.
items.answer_explanation: Information is uncountable, so much is the appropriate quantifier.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: much modifies the uncountable noun information.

items.subtype: adverb required to modify a following finite verb
items.stem: The filter operates ___ when the input signal contains background noise.
items.answer_explanation: An adverb is required to modify the finite verb operates.

distractor_rationales.A: The adjective cannot directly modify operates.
distractor_rationales.B: The noun cannot modify the verb.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: efficiently is the adverb modifying operates.
distractor_rationales.D: The comparative adjective lacks a comparison and the required adverbial function.

items.subtype: article before a singular count noun
items.sentence: An ecosystem supports many forms of life.
items.answer_explanation: The article an correctly precedes the singular count noun ecosystem.

items.subtype: simple past in a dated historical sequence
items.sentence: The railway opened the mountain route in 1898.
items.answer_explanation: The dated event correctly uses the simple past.

items.subtype: adjective modifying a research noun
items.sentence: The study reports significant changes in memory.
items.answer_explanation: The adjective significant correctly modifies the noun changes.

items.subtype: quantifier with a plural count noun
items.sentence: Several methods improve the harvest yield.
items.minimal_correction: D: the harvest yield → the harvest yields
items.answer_explanation: The planned correction makes the quantified count noun plural.

items.subtype: parallel gerund phrases after a coordinator
items.sentence: The course emphasizes reading critically and writing clearly.
items.answer_explanation: The two gerund phrases are parallel after emphasizes.

items.subtype: adjective complement after a linking verb
items.sentence: The plateau appears stable during the dry season.
items.answer_explanation: Appears correctly takes the predicate adjective stable.

items.subtype: gerund as the object of a preposition
items.sentence: Scientists are committed to protecting the coral reef.
items.answer_explanation: The preposition to is correctly followed by the gerund protecting.

items.subtype: relative pronoun as the subject of a restrictive clause
items.sentence: The arch that supports the roof was recently repaired.
items.minimal_correction: D: was recently repaired → was recently repaired
items.answer_explanation: That correctly serves as the subject of the restrictive relative clause.

items.subtype: adverb modifying a participle
items.sentence: The rapidly moving clouds covered the horizon.
items.answer_explanation: Rapidly is the adverb modifying moving.

items.subtype: preposition selected for a noun phrase
items.sentence: Investors are concerned about the sudden change.
items.answer_explanation: Concerned correctly combines with the preposition about.

items.subtype: pronoun agreement with a singular antecedent
items.sentence: Each participant submitted their questionnaire before leaving.
items.minimal_correction: C: their questionnaire → his or her questionnaire
items.answer_explanation: The singular antecedent each participant requires a singular pronoun in the locked construction.

items.subtype: parallel noun phrases after both and
items.sentence: The survey measured both public trust and policy awareness.
items.minimal_correction: D: and policy awareness → and policy awareness
items.answer_explanation: Both coordinates the parallel noun phrases public trust and policy awareness.

items.subtype: passive voice with an object receiving an action
items.sentence: The vaccine was tested on volunteers before approval.
items.answer_explanation: The vaccine correctly receives the action in the passive construction.

items.subtype: adjective phrase in postmodifier position
items.sentence: The poems written during exile reveal a new style.
items.minimal_correction: B: written during exile → written during exile
items.answer_explanation: The participial adjective phrase correctly follows and modifies poems.

items.subtype: present participle in a reduced active clause
items.sentence: Using infrared sensors, the robot avoids obstacles.
items.answer_explanation: Using correctly introduces a reduced active clause whose understood subject is the robot.

items.subtype: definite article for a uniquely identified institution
items.sentence: The court published its decision on Monday.
items.minimal_correction: D: on Monday → on the Monday
items.answer_explanation: The planned correction supplies the definite article in the marked institutional time phrase.

items.subtype: comparative adjective with than
items.sentence: The second estimate is more precise than the first.
items.minimal_correction: A: The second estimate → The second estimate
items.answer_explanation: More precise correctly forms the comparative with than.

items.subtype: verb governed by an infinitive complement
items.sentence: The device allows operators to adjust the pressure.
items.answer_explanation: Allow correctly takes an object followed by an infinitive complement.

items.subtype: parallel finite verbs coordinated by and
items.sentence: The conductor raised the baton and began the performance.
items.minimal_correction: C: raised the baton and began → raised the baton and began
items.answer_explanation: Raised and began are parallel finite verbs coordinated by and.

items.subtype: noun required as the object of a preposition
items.sentence: The artifact provides evidence of early settlement.
items.answer_explanation: Settlement is the noun required after the preposition of.

items.subtype: whose for a possessive relative relationship
items.sentence: The star whose spectrum changed was observed again.
items.answer_explanation: Whose correctly marks the possessive relationship between star and spectrum.

items.subtype: although introducing a finite concessive clause
items.sentence: Although costs increased, the program continued to expand.
items.answer_explanation: Although correctly introduces the finite concessive clause.

items.subtype: past perfect before a later past event
items.sentence: The patient had recovered before the physician arrived.
items.answer_explanation: Had recovered correctly marks the earlier of the two past events.

items.subtype: few with a plural count noun
items.sentence: Few residents opposed the construction plan.
items.minimal_correction: D: the construction plan → the construction plans
items.answer_explanation: The planned correction makes the quantified count noun plural.

items.subtype: infinitive of purpose before a main clause
items.sentence: To reduce emissions, the city expanded its solar program.
items.minimal_correction: A: To reduce emissions → To reduce emissions
items.answer_explanation: The infinitive phrase correctly expresses the purpose of the main clause.
